routes.name: EU/EEA free movement and residence
routes.summary: EU nationals don't need a permit to live and work in Malta. EEA nationals can stay while working, self-employed, self-sufficient, studying or as family members.

other: Rights can be limited on public policy, security or health grounds, or if you become an unreasonable burden on Malta's social assistance system.

routes.name: Residence permits for non-EU nationals (overview)
routes.summary: Non-EU nationals need a residence permit from Identita's Expatriates Unit. Employment permits and non-employment permits (family, study, self-sufficient, long-term) each have their own pages.

other: Employment must be in Malta. The permit does not give you the right to work elsewhere in the EU.

routes.name: Single Permit (work and residence)
routes.summary: One application covers the employment license and residence permit for non-EU workers with a Maltese employer, for over 6 months. Employer sponsored and tied to that employer and job.

other: Holders can't work for other parties or do work outside the job in the application.
Applications go through the employer, with checks by Identita, Jobsplus and the Police.
Fee, salary and processing details are on sub-pages that did not load, so none are stated.

routes.name: Seasonal Worker permit
routes.summary: For seasonal work stays over 90 days, via the single application with an employer in Malta. You must keep your main home outside Malta.

other: Fixed-term contract directly with a Maltese employer.

fees.label: Single permit application for seasonal workers

routes.name: Intra-Corporate Transferee permit
routes.summary: Temporary secondment of a non-EU employee from a company outside Malta (or in another EU state) to a Maltese entity of the same group.

other: Governed by S.L. 217.21. Conditions are on a sub-page that did not load.

stay.note: Fees are listed for up to three years of permit duration.

fees.label: Renewal, per year of permit (up to three years)

routes.name: Self-employment residence permit
routes.summary: Self-employed non-EU nationals first need an employment licence from Jobsplus, then apply to Identita. Directors and shareholders doing executive work for a registered company count as employees and need a Single Permit instead.

other: Apply for the Jobsplus employment licence first.
At renewal you can ask for a 3-year permit if the licence covers it.

fees.label: Renewal, per year of permit (up to three years)

routes.name: Blue Card, Key Employment and Specialist Employee initiatives
routes.summary: Identita lists the Blue Card, Key Employment Initiative and Specialist Employee Initiative for highly qualified workers. Thresholds and conditions were not on the pages that loaded.

other: Salary and qualification rules were not confirmed. Check Identita's Highly Qualified Individuals page.

routes.name: Nomad Residence Permit
routes.summary: One-year permit for non-EU remote workers who keep a job, business or freelance clients outside Malta. Renewable at the agency's discretion.

income.note: Gross. Applications before 1 April 2024 keep the old 32,400 EUR threshold. Income must be guaranteed for at least 5 months from the application date.

other: Work for a foreign employer, own a share in a foreign company you work for, or freelance for foreign clients under contract.
You can't serve a Maltese subsidiary or Maltese clients.
Valid property rental or purchase agreement for the whole permit.
Health insurance covering Malta, the EU and the UK.
Police conduct certificate and background check.

The FAQ lists ineligible nationals or close ties: Afghanistan, North Korea, Iran, DR Congo, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Yemen, Venezuela, and applications from Russia and Belarus. The agency can change the list.
Renewals need 5 months of residence in the last 12 months.

steps: Submit the application through the Residency Malta portal
After approval in principle, send proof of accommodation and health insurance
documents: Police conduct certificate under 6 months old
Employment contract, company documents or service contracts

routes.name: Malta Startup Residence Programme
routes.summary: 3-year residence permit for non-EU founders, co-founders, core employees and their families, extendable for 5 more years. You need a real presence in Malta and pay tax locally.

other: Founders build an innovative startup or scale-up in Malta. Malta Enterprise is the contact point for support.
Fees and detailed criteria were not on the page read.

routes.name: Malta Permanent Residence Programme (MPRP)
routes.summary: Residency by investment for non-EU, non-EEA, non-Swiss nationals. You must apply through a licensed agent. It gives permanent residence, not citizenship.

savings.note: Capital assets of at least 500,000 EUR with 150,000 EUR financial, or at least 650,000 EUR with 75,000 EUR financial.

other: Stable and regular resources without using Malta's social assistance.
Clean criminal record, no security risk.
Not from a country the agency lists as sanctioned.
Rent a home for at least 14,000 EUR a year, or buy one worth at least 375,000 EUR. Keep it 5 years, then keep a home in Malta.
Donate 2,000 EUR to a registered local NGO.
Health insurance covering Malta and Europe.

fees.label: Residence card, per person, covers 5 years

routes.name: Family member residence permit
routes.summary: Family of someone with a Maltese residence permit can get a permit for family reunification under S.L. 217.06. Others may qualify under the family members policy.

other: The sponsor already holds a residence permit in Malta.
Apply online through the Expatriates Portal. Passport needs 6 months validity.

routes.name: Study, research, training and volunteer permits
routes.summary: Residence permit for full-time study at an institution licensed by the National Commission for Higher Education, plus research, training and volunteering. Visa-exempt students must apply within 3 months of entering the EU.

other: The course must lead to a higher education qualification recognized at MQF level 5, or be a preparatory programme for one.
Students needing a visa must hold an education visa.
Apply in person in Malta. Passport needs 6 months validity.
Students at the University of Malta, MCAST or ITS are exempt from the health insurance requirement.

sources.label: Identita: Study, Research, Trainees, Volunteers and Interns

routes.name: Economic self-sufficiency permit (retirement, passive income)
routes.summary: Temporary permit for third-country nationals who can support themselves. You need valid authorization to be in Malta first. Identita points to the Global Residence Programme, MPRP, Malta Retirement Programme and citizenship holders.

other: You must already hold a valid visa or residence permit for Malta.
Apply online through the Expatriates Portal. Passport needs 6 months validity.
Income thresholds were not stated on the page.

routes.name: Long-term residence status
routes.summary: Permanent status for third-country nationals after 5 years of legal, continuous residence. The card is valid for 5 years.

other: 5 years or more of legal and continuous residence in Malta.
Stable and regular resources and your own accommodation.
Meet the integration measures in S.L. 217.05.
Apply online. Passport needs 6 months validity.

routes.name: Schengen, National and Student visas
routes.summary: Malta's Central Visa Unit handles short stay Schengen visas (up to 90 days in 180) and airport transit visas, plus National and Student visas.

other: Who needs a visa, fees and documents were not confirmed. Check the Central Visa Unit pages and the EU visa-free list.

sources.label: Identita: Central Visa Unit fees and applications

routes.name: Citizenship by naturalisation (residence)
routes.summary: Adults can apply after living in Malta for the last 12 months and 4 of the 6 years before that. The Minister decides at their discretion.

eligibility.language: Adequate knowledge of Maltese or English
other: Good character and a suitable citizen.
Two sponsors who are not relatives, signing in front of a witness.
Oath of allegiance.
Book a residence certificate appointment before applying.
The agency's page does not mention a citizenship test.

citizenship.note: Malta allows dual citizenship. Check whether your home country does.

routes.name: Citizenship by registration (spouse)
routes.summary: Spouses of Maltese citizens can register after 5 years of marriage, if still married and living together. Widows and widowers can also apply in set cases.

other: Joint affidavit that you have been married 5 years and live together.
Marriage certificate registered in Malta.

routes.name: Citizenship by birth and descent
routes.summary: Born abroad on or after 1 August 1989 to a Maltese parent who is a citizen by birth in Malta, naturalisation or registration: automatic citizen. Citizenship doesn't pass on from a parent who registered based on descent. Later generations can register under the registration route.

other: Descendants in the direct line of an ascendant born in Malta to a parent also born in Malta can register (Forms K and M).
The July 2025 amendments changed the rules on when the descent link is severed after a parent's death. Check Komunita for details.

citizenship.note: Dual citizenship has been allowed since 10 February 2000.
